findings.summary: 86Box is an IBM PC emulator derived from PCem that runs legacy operating systems and software on Windows, Linux, and macOS. It emulates x86 processors from 8088 through Pentium MMX and Pentium Pro/II, along with graphics modes (CGA, EGA, VGA, VESA, Glide) and sound cards (Sound Blaster, AdLib, AWE32, etc.). It supports MS-DOS, Windows up to 7, OS/2, Linux, BSD, and BeOS on specific hardware. A built-in VM manager was added in version 5.0.

mechanisms.title: Processor emulation and recompilation
mechanisms.explanation: 86Box emulates Intel and compatible x86 processors (8088 through Pentium MMX, Pentium Pro/II). A mandatory recompiler is used for Pentium and Cyrix processors, while it is optional for i486 and WinChip. This allows accurate execution of legacy software on modern host hardware.

mechanisms.title: Graphics and video subsystem emulation
mechanisms.explanation: The emulator supports text mode and multiple graphics adapters (Hercules, CGA, EGA, VGA, Mode X, VESA) and video APIs (DirectX, Glide). Specific hardware cards such as ATI Mach64, S3 Trio, and Voodoo 1/2/3 are emulated; a separate recompiler improves Voodoo performance.
